cau.<strong1>Ăn vặt Đà Lạt buổi tối</strong1: <strong1>Evening street food in Da Lat</strong1> in a nutshell: head to the night market in the city center, where the stalls set up along both sides of the street at dusk and sell until late. The fifteen dishes most worth trying are bánh tráng nướng (grilled rice paper), bánh căn (mini rice cakes), bánh mì xíu mại (meatball soup with bread), nem nướng (grilled pork sausage), grilled skewers, grilled corn with scallion oil, snails, bánh ướt lòng gà (rice sheets with chicken giblets), bánh bèo chén (steamed rice cakes in small bowls), bánh tráng trộn (rice paper salad), hot soy milk, hot chè (sweet soup), avocado ice cream, cheese yogurt and crushed strawberries. cau.Buổi chiều thư giãn ở một quán cafe view: Relax in the afternoon at a café overlooking the pine forest. In the evening, stroll Da Lat Night Market for grilled rice paper ("Da Lat pizza"), snails and hot soy milk — and end the day with a warm cup of soy milk in the cool night air.
cau.Buổi sáng dành cho phở gà Đà Lạt — nước: Spend the morning on Da Lat chicken phở — crystal-clear broth and firm free-range chicken — then head out to explore the outskirts: valleys, the Cau Dat tea hills, or some light trekking. For lunch, be sure to try chicken hotpot with é leaves, free-range chicken cooked with fragrant é leaves (Trạm Dừng Chill also serves Chicken Hotpot with É Leaves at 300,000 VND a pot, but the restaurant opens at 15:00, so you can only have it for a late-afternoon or evening meal).

Prices outside the restaurant vary by season and by seller, so we don't give specific figures — we only cover how to choose and how to keep your gifts from spoiling on the way home.

cau.Chợ đêm không có giờ giấc chung: mỗi quầ: The night market has no shared opening hours: each stall sets up and packs up on its own schedule, depending on the season and the weather. The most pleasant time to go is <strong1>after dinner</strong1>, when most stalls are out but it isn't too crowded yet; the later it gets, the thinner it becomes, as many stalls sell out early, though weekends usually run later. The snacks here are everyday food — each portion is small and much cheaper than a main meal — but prices change with the season and from vendor to vendor, so ask before you order.
cau.Chợ đêm Đà Lạt họp ngay khu chợ Đà Lạt,: Da Lat Night Market sets up right around Da Lat Market. It's busiest early in the evening and then thins out depending on the weather and the season — each stall packs up at a different time, so don't leave it too late. You'll find snacks, woolens, local produce and candied fruit to take home as gifts. Prices are affordable, but they vary from stall to stall and change with the season, so ask before you order. It gets very crowded on weekends; if you're in a group, agree on a meeting point beforehand.

cau.Các quầy ăn vặt quanh chợ Đà Lạt dọn ra: The snack stalls around Da Lat Market set up from dusk and sell until late, with no fixed shared hours — every stall is different, and it also depends on the season and the weather. The most pleasant time is after dinner, when nearly all the stalls are out but it isn't too crowded yet. The later it gets, the more stalls are selling off their last stock; weekends are usually busier and run later than weekdays.
cau.Cách chắc ăn nhất là đến khoảng 16:00 và: The surest plan is to arrive around 16:00 and book ahead. cau.Cắm trại ở Đà Lạt khác trước hết ở cái l: The first thing that sets camping in Da Lat apart is the cold. Sitting on a plateau at about 1,500 meters, <a1>Da Lat</a1> has a mild climate all year round: the daytime sun is very pleasant, but as soon as it sets the temperature drops fast — in the dry season, the average nighttime low in town is only about 11–13°C (December to March, months 12–3, according to the climate table on the Wikipedia page linked above), and it's colder still up high and by the lakes. Many first-timers see the blazing midday sun, pack only a light jacket, and end up huddled and shivering late at night.
cau.Cắm trại ở Đà Lạt không cần thiết bị đắt: Camping in Da Lat doesn't require expensive gear or survival skills. Pick the right season, bring enough warm layers, respect the forest and the people who live nearby — the city takes care of the rest: pine trees, mist, and a morning when you open your tent to find the clouds lying right at your feet.

cau.Hồng treo gió khác hồng sấy thường ở chỗ: How are wind-dried persimmons different from regular dried persimmons?
cau.Hồng treo gió được gọt vỏ rồi treo cho g: Wind-dried persimmons are peeled and then hung up so the cold wind dries them naturally instead of a machine, which leaves the flesh dense and chewy, deeply sweet, with a thin dusting of natural sugar on the outside. Machine drying is much faster, so machine-dried persimmons are drier in texture and milder in flavor. Because they take more work and lose more fruit in the process, wind-dried persimmons usually cost more than machine-dried ones; how much more depends on the seller and the season.
cau.Hồng Đà Lạt được gọt vỏ rồi treo cho gió: Da Lat persimmons are peeled and hung so the cold wind slowly dries them, using a Japanese-style technique, and a batch takes quite a while depending on the weather. The finished fruit has a thin coating of natural sugar bloom on the outside and is dense and chewy inside, deeply sweet without being cloying. It's the most labor-intensive item on this list, so it usually costs more than machine-dried persimmons; prices vary by season and by seller, so ask at a few places to compare.
